Congratulations to Pippa Hackett 
Congratulations 
to 
Greens 
Party 
representative Pippa Hackett on her 
election to the Seanad Eireann on 1st 
November. Ms Hackett, the party’s 
agriculture spokeswoman, was elected to 
the vacant seat left by colleague Grace 
O’Sullivan, who was elected to the 
European Parliament in May. Ms Hackett 
was the first Green councillor elected to 
Offaly County Council in May.

FIRE AND EMERGENCY SERVICES 
General Updates 
A Major Emergency Exercise took place 
on the 16th October in Tullamore.  The 
Offaly County Council Major Emergency 
Plan, the use of the temporary onsite 
coordination centre, the local coordination 
centre, and the Tetra communication 
network were all tested as part of the 
exercise.   
 
Over 80 participants were involved from An 
Garda Síochána, the HSE and Offaly County 
Council.  Fire crews from Longford, 
Westmeath, and Laois supported Offaly Fire 
& Rescue Service on the incident ground.  
The exercise was coordinated by the Midland 
Regional 
Working 
Group 
for 
Major 
Emergency Management  
 
Offaly County Council was the Lead Agency 
for the exercise incident with the Local Co-
ordination 
Group 
being 
chaired 
and 
coordinated by CEO Anna-Marie Delaney. 
 
 
 
National Fire Safety Week took place from 
6th - 13th October 2019.  During October, 
firefighters from Offaly delivered the 
“Schools Fire Safety Programme” to 
approximately 1,800 3rd class children in 
Offaly primary schools. 
 
1916 Commemorative Medals will be 
presented in the coming weeks to all 
members, both past and present, who served 
with Offaly County Council Fire & Rescue 
Service in 2016.

Comhairle na n’Óg: 
The 2019 Comhairle Na NÓg AGM took 
place on Tuesday 15th October. The day was 
a great success with over 200 young people 
attending on the day. The theme of the day 
was ‘Less Stress More Success’ and centred 
around the 2019 project topic ‘Exam Stress 
& Anxiety’. The Comhairle Executive 
unveiled an information booklet listing a 
series of tips for coping with exam stress 
which was launched on the day by the 
Cathaoirleach, Cllr Peter Ormond.  
The second series of events relating to the 
project took place in the afternoon through 
two workshops run by Leinster Rugby 
representatives led by Patsy Gorman and a 
motivational Speaker Dave Russell. A 
number of Youth Service organisations i.e. 
Jigsaw, the EDAN Project, Gardaí were also 
represented on the day to support and offer 
advice to young people. 
There was a fantastic atmosphere in the room 
on the day with spot prizes and goody bags 
on offer. There was tremendous engagement 
by the young people with 31 expressions of

LIBRARY SERVICES 
Children’s Book Festival – Offaly Success 
With 92 reading development events and 
an attendance of over 1,853, Offaly’s 
Children’s Book Festival (CBF) was a huge 
success.  As part of the Right to Read 
national programme, there were targets set 
for the first time for CBF, which Offaly 
comfortably exceeded. With 22,374 visits to 
Offaly library branches in October, this 
festival was well supported by the Offaly 
community.

Service projects from

Autism Friendly Offaly Libraries  
As part of the programme, there were public 
and staff autism awareness training sessions 
and a series of sensory story-times with a 
qualified play therapist in four locations, 
Birr, Clara, Edenderry and Tullamore. All 19 
sessions were fully booked.  These sessions 
allowed teachers and special needs assistants 
(SNA) to discuss sensory programming with 
the facilitator. 
AsIAm will conduct a sensory audit on two of 
our libraries during November which will 
enable Offaly Libraries be recognised as a 
registered business certified with the AsIAm 
Autism Friendly Business Award.  A 
garden designer will also create a sensory 
garden plan, planting list and guidelines for 
maintenance which will help inform Stage 2 
in the Autism Friendly accreditation process.

LOCAL ENTERPRISE OFFICE 
National Women's Enterprise Day!  
The largest-ever programme of events for 
National Women’s Enterprise Day has taken 
place across the country this week (on 
October 17th). The theme for this year’s 
event was “Making It Happen” with the aim 
of inspiring more women in Ireland to start 
and grow their own business. 
 
 
 
The networking event for entrepreneurs in 
the Midland region took place in Gloster 
House, Birr and was organised in partnership 
with Local Enterprise Offices in Laois, 
Longford, Offaly and Westmeath. Over 125 
local entrepreneurs and businesswomen 
participated and speakers included Colette 
Twomey, Clonakilty Food Company Ltd; 
Louise Lennox (of the Restaurant); Emma 
Rose Conroy of Euro Stallions (NWED 
Ambassador); Ellen Gunning, Academy of 
Public Relations and Anna Marie Delaney, 
CE, Offaly County Council, MC for the 
event was Susan Keogh, Newstalk.

Creating Economic & Business 
Opportunities from Climate Change 
The “Creating Economic and Business 
Opportunities 
from 
Climate 
Change” 
conference took place in the Tullamore Court 
Hotel on Wednesday 9th of October. The 
conference room was full with over 150 
people attending the event, the first of its’ 
kind to be hosted in the Midlands, and it did 
not disappoint. The conference, an initiative 
of the Regional Transition Team under the 
auspices 
of 
the 
Midlands 
Regional 
Enterprise Plan to 2020 (MREP), explored 
how businesses can realise unique economic 
and business opportunities in responding to 
climate change.  
The conference marked the commencement 
of discussions on Creating Economic and 
Business 
Opportunities 
from 
Climate 
Change, examining international trends, and 
exploring how responses to climate change, 
by both business and communities, can 
effectively drive innovation, adoption of 
disruptive technologies, and more flexible 
work practices. 
 
 
The Keynote Speaker for the event was Dr. 
Tara Shine, Environmental Scientist and 
Director, Change by Degrees.  She is an 
environmental scientist with over 20 years’ 
experience working as an adviser to 
governments and world leaders. Other 
speakers were Ron Immink, Sustainable 
Nation, Dr Shane Ward, Professor of 
Biosystems Engineering in UCD, Deirdre 
DeBhailis, Dingle Hub, Dr. Joanne Rourke, 
Eastern and Midlands Regional Waste 
Management, 
Paddy 
Matthews, 
Fáilte 
Ireland and MC Jonathon Healy, Newstalk. 
The event was recorded and is available at: 
https://www.facebook.com/MidlandsIreland
.ie/videos/898108173895892/

Productivity Voucher 
The Productivity Voucher is a national 
programme that supports Ireland’s small 
businesses and enterprises, by providing 
them with the right advice and training 
resources to enhance productivity and 
efficiency. 
Small 
Irish 
businesses 
or 
enterprises can now apply for one of 200 
productivity vouchers valued at €2,500 each, 
to help them develop a more efficient and 
productive business operation. It aims to 
increase your business productivity in any of 
the following ways: 
 Improve the quality of your products 
 Reduce your delivery times 
 Lower your costs of production 
 Reduce waste in your business 
 Increase your ability to generate 
more revenue 
The Productivity voucher can be used by 
participating in small businesses to: 
 Engage and leverage experts, who 
can consult with you and help you 
assess your business’ value chain and 
operations.  
 Invest in training & capability 
development. It will support the 
development of a more effective, 
capable and efficient workforce 
through relevant training.
